_format: Sample questions written for testing. Faisal's real mark-scheme data replaces these. Each point is one mark: it is earned when the answer contains at least one phrase from EVERY group in 'match'.

questions.question: Explain how a negative number is stored using two's complement.

points.text: The most significant bit has a negative place value / is the sign bit
To negate: invert / flip all the bits
...then add 1

questions.question: Explain the difference between lossy and lossless compression.

points.text: Lossy permanently removes / discards data
Lossless lets the original file be reconstructed exactly
Example of a lossless technique: run-length encoding

questions.question: Describe the differences between a LAN and a WAN.

points.text: A LAN covers a small geographical area (e.g. one building / site)
A WAN covers a large geographical area
A WAN uses third-party / leased communication links; a LAN's infrastructure is owned by the organisation

questions.question: Explain the role of DNS when a user types a URL into a browser.

points.text: The browser sends the domain name / URL to a DNS server
The DNS server looks up the matching IP address
If not found, the request is passed to another (higher-level) DNS server
The IP address is returned to the browser so it can contact the web server

questions.question: State the differences between SRAM and DRAM.

points.text: DRAM must be refreshed; SRAM does not
SRAM is faster to access
DRAM is cheaper / has higher density
SRAM is used for cache memory

questions.question: Explain how a laser printer prints a page.

points.text: A laser draws the image onto a charged drum
The charge is removed where the laser hits / an electrostatic image forms
Toner sticks to the charged areas of the drum
The toner is transferred to paper and fused with heat

questions.question: Describe the fetch stage of the fetch-execute cycle using register transfer notation or words.

points.text: The address in the PC is copied to the MAR
The PC is incremented
The instruction at that address is copied into the MDR
The contents of the MDR are copied to the CIR

questions.question: Explain what an interrupt is and how the processor handles it.

points.text: An interrupt is a signal from a device / program asking for the processor's attention
The processor checks for interrupts at the end of each fetch-execute cycle
The current register contents are saved (e.g. on a stack)
The interrupt service routine (ISR) is run
The saved values are restored and the original task resumes

questions.question: Compare a compiler and an interpreter.

points.text: A compiler translates the whole program at once before running
An interpreter translates and executes one line / statement at a time
A compiler produces an executable file / object code
An interpreter stops at the first error, making debugging easier

questions.question: State three tasks carried out by an operating system.

points.text: Memory management
Process management / scheduling
File management
Security management (e.g. user accounts)
Hardware / peripheral management (drivers)

questions.question: Explain the difference between data validation and data verification.

points.text: Validation checks that data is reasonable / sensible / meets rules
Validation cannot check the data is correct
Verification checks data has been copied / entered accurately (matches the original)
Example method: double entry / visual check / parity check / checksum

questions.question: Explain how a firewall helps protect a network.

points.text: It sits between the network and the internet / external network
It inspects incoming and outgoing traffic / packets
It blocks traffic that doesn't meet a set of rules / criteria

questions.question: Explain the difference between free software and freeware.

points.text: Free software gives users the freedom to view and modify the source code
Free software can be redistributed (possibly modified)
Freeware costs nothing but the source code is not available / cannot be modified

questions.question: Explain why a software developer should follow a professional code of conduct such as the BCS or IEEE code.

points.text: To act in the public interest / protect public safety
To act honestly / with integrity towards clients and employers
To maintain and develop their professional competence

questions.question: Explain what is meant by a primary key and a foreign key.

points.text: A primary key uniquely identifies each record / tuple in a table
A foreign key is an attribute in one table that is the primary key of another table
Foreign keys are used to create relationships between tables

questions.question: Explain what is needed for a table to be in third normal form (3NF).

points.text: The table is in 2NF (and therefore 1NF)
There are no non-key dependencies / transitive dependencies
Every non-key attribute depends only on the primary key

questions.question: Describe how a linear search works.

points.text: Start at the first element
Compare each element in turn with the item being searched for
Stop when the item is found
...or when the end of the list is reached (item not present)

questions.question: Explain why abstraction and decomposition are useful when solving a problem.

points.text: Abstraction removes unnecessary detail / keeps only what is relevant
Decomposition breaks the problem into smaller sub-problems
Smaller parts are easier to solve / test / can be shared between programmers

questions.question: Explain how a stack works and state one use of a stack.

points.text: A stack is LIFO (last in, first out)
Items are pushed onto / popped off the top
A pointer keeps track of the top of the stack
A use: interrupt handling / procedure calls / reversing data / undo

questions.question: Explain what a record data type is and why it is useful.

points.text: A record is a composite / user-defined data type
It groups several related fields / items of data
The fields can be of different data types

questions.question: Explain the difference between passing a parameter by value and by reference.

points.text: By value: a copy of the data is passed
By value: changes in the procedure do not affect the original variable
By reference: the address of / a pointer to the variable is passed
By reference: changes in the procedure change the original variable

questions.question: Explain the difference between a procedure and a function.

points.text: A function returns a value
A procedure does not return a value
A function call can be used in an expression / assignment

questions.question: Describe the stages of the waterfall model and one drawback of it.

points.text: Stages run in order: analysis, design, coding, testing, maintenance
Each stage must be completed before the next begins
Drawback: hard to go back / change requirements; working software only appears late

questions.question: Explain the difference between white-box and black-box testing.

points.text: White-box testing uses knowledge of the code / tests every path
Black-box testing only checks inputs against expected outputs
Black-box testers do not look at the code
